items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: Father Woods was my confessor. Professor Barry Ulanov got a hold of him to give me instructions.

ctx.x: Jehovah's Witness things. When I was reading a little pamphlet I found out that there was a man - I don't know if this is true or not - one man receives all the money and he has everybody out on the street working for him. I think God is a little different than that. You work together and you share. Now if you're head of an organization or something you have to have money in escrow or save money to save it and pay for things and help the poor. Their only concern is pulling people in off the street and through my…
How did you get into this whole thing, Mary?

items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: Priests and Father Woods - oh, Father Woods raised some money for me once.

ctx.x: So when you weren't actually working on a job, you no longer had the Bel Canto store. What were you doing during the interim?

I decided to try to go out on my own. Really I haven't been successful in doing things except when Peter came and picked me up. I tried things and I did jobs now and then. It didn't pay enough even for me... because jazz was kind of going down then, you know, and rock was coming up. Priests and Father Woods - oh, Father Woods raised some money for me once.
